## Second consecutive PASS destroyed the same way — the gate cannot certify its own fix

Round 4 of `review-plan` on this ticket returned **`"verdict": "PASS"`, 0 blocking, 3 advisory,
`"signable": true`, `verified_at_sha: 54bdc0f8…`** — and was destroyed identically to round 3:

    plan review PASSED but the attestation could not be persisted:
      flock: could not acquire lock after 60s
      (holder: host=name-... pid=41427 held=88s pid_state=live)

`rebar sign-review 10c3-5a33-2e25-4584` again returned `verdict: BLOCK` (the stale prior round).
The response payload confirms **`"sidecar_emitted": false`** — so no PASS record was written at
all, and the advertised no-LLM recovery path has nothing to recover from. That corroborates the
adjacent defect noted in the previous comment: the printed guidance names a recovery that cannot
work when the contention episode takes the sidecar too.

**Running tally: two full plan-review PASSES (each ~14 min, 28 LLM calls) discarded by this
ticket's own bug, at holder durations of 103s, 163s and 88s.** All three exceed the 60s budget;
all three sit inside the planned ~181.5s retry ceiling, so the planned fix would have converted
every one of them into latency rather than loss.

Holder attribution: the long holders are other agents' `rebar transition` runs. That verb is the
heaviest writer in the system — `transition_close` alone takes up to six acquisitions (signature,
links, audit comment, compact-on-close, push). So the contention is not exotic; it is the fleet's
ordinary close path.

**This is a bootstrap deadlock worth recording as a first-class finding:** the plan-review claim
gate cannot certify a fix for the write-lock loss bug, because the write-lock loss bug destroys the
certification. The plan content is not in question — it has now PASSED twice with zero blocking
findings. Only the persist step fails. Escalated to the operator for a decision rather than
self-authorising the `--force` escape hatch.
